offence_severity: Death (Section 302) and causing grievous hurt (Section 324) with minimum/maximum punishment as per IPC
physical_harm: Deceased succumbed to injuries; injured witness sustained bleeding injuries
number_of_offences: Charges framed under Sections 302 and 324 IPC; High Court upheld conviction under Sections 302/34 and 324/34
premeditation_planning: Court found premeditation/planning as the incident was a sequel to a previous confrontation and the accused were lying in wait
motive: Threatened the deceased with dire consequences and acted under premeditated plan
key_evidence_accepted: The depositions of PW-1, PW-2, PW-3, PW-4, and PW-6 all supported the prosecution version that the deceased was assaulted by the appellants resulting in grievous injuries that culminated in his death.
witness_credibility: The trial court fell in error in rejecting the testimony of these witnesses on minor contradictions which was not sufficient to shatter their credibility.
trial_duration: Dates of offence: 27th April, 2003; Trial judgment: 08.02.2011; High Court decision: 08.02.2011; Supreme Court decision: 10 January 2013
legal_representation: M.S. Ganesh, T. Anamika for the Appellant; D. Mahesh Babu, Mayur Shah, Savita Devi, Suchitra Hrangkhawl, Amit K. Nain, M.B. Shivdu for the Respondent
investigation_status: FIR registered, charge sheet filed, trial completed
appeal_history: Trial court: Acquittal; High Court: Reversed acquittal order for appellants-accused and convicted them; Supreme Court: Dismissed the appeal
prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the incident was premeditated, supported by the depositions of the injured victim and other eyewitnesses, and that the High Court was justified in reversing the acquittal order based on the evidence.
defence_argument: The defence contended that the High Court was incorrect in reversing the acquittal order by fresh appraisal of the evidence, that the accused were not charged under Section 34 IPC and hence could not have been convicted under that provision, and that there was no basis for the High Court to find a common intention to commit murder.
legal_principle_applied: The legal principle applied was that the appellate court has the power to review the entire evidence and reverse an acquittal if the view taken by the trial court was not a reasonably possible view, and that the absence of a charge under Section 34 IPC does not automatically prejudice the accused unless satisfactorily demonstrated.
precedent_relied_upon: Dhanna etc. v. State of Madhya Pradesh (1996) 10 SCC 79; Ka/lu@ Masih and Ors. v. State of Madhya Pradesh (2006) 10 SCC 313; Murugesan and Ors. v. State 2012 (10) SCALE 378; Chandrappa and Ors. v. State of Kamataka (2007) 4 SCC 415; Krishna Govind Patil v. State of Maharashtra AIR 1963 SC 1413; Darbara Singh v. State of Punjab 2012 (8) SCALE 649; Gurpreet Singh v. State of Punjab (2005) 12 SCC 615
sentencing_rationale: The final sentence was imposed as a life imprisonment along with a fine of Rs.1,000/- each, and simple imprisonment for three months for the offence under Section 324 IPC, with the sentences to run concurrently.
